status: prospective controlled-mechanism experiment locked before outcome execution; synthetic finite-support stress test, not heldout LLM evidence
research_question: At equal policy KL and fixed verifier-error norm, does verifier-error alignment control whether proxy improvement becomes true regression?
true_reward: Bernoulli(0.5) per support item, resampled deterministically until both classes occur
error_construction: p-centered unit vector u orthogonal to centered standardized reward; e = sigma * (rho * y_std + sqrt(1-rho^2) * u)
optimizer: q_beta(i) proportional to p(i) exp(beta v(i)); beta inverted independently to match KL(q||p)
local_geometry_prediction: for beta -> 0+, sign true_progress = sign Cov_p(y,v) = sign(1 + sigma*rho), since y_std has unit p-variance and u is p-orthogonal
primary_prediction: excluding exact boundary cells with 1+sigma*rho=0, the sign of mean true_progress by (sigma,rho) agrees with sign(1+sigma*rho) in at least 90% of cells; proxy_progress remains nonnegative
paired_intervention: within each task seed, baseline p, reward y, orthogonal direction u, sigma and KL are held fixed while only rho changes
reporting: retain all task/config rows; report phase accuracy, false-progress rate, mean true/proxy progress, and paired harmful-minus-benign contrasts without variant selection
scope: mechanism identification only; no pretrained model, no learned verifier, no claim of frontier-model improvement or deployment safety
